title: Signal Lichen: catalogue and actionable fragments
body:
Purpose: quick synthesis of recent field interviews (Aug 2027) + compact set of prioritized asks with proposed engineers-friendly micro-solutions. Audience: product leads (hosted & dedicated), serving-runtime eng, and solutions eng. This is intentionally short — use as a handoff for sprint spikes.

Summary of signal themes (high-level):
1) Operational visibility gaps (KV cache, per-route token breakdowns, and cold-start granularity). Multiple customers report they can’t correlate customer-side latency spikes with specific cache-miss patterns; they want per-route and per-customer cache hit rates surfaced to the Console and API.
2) Dedicated autoscaling surprise behavior. Customers with bursty workloads saw queue growth when ephemeral burst nodes spun up because routing policies favored warm nodes in other regions. They ask for predictable short-burst capacity and a clearer SLA for burst activation time.
3) Inference cost unpredictability tied to quantization fallbacks. Several infra teams noted that when the runtime falls back from 4-bit quantized kernels to higher precision due to sequence-length/attention patterns, token cost and latency jump unpredictably. They want an opt-in “strict-quantization” policy plus instrumentation.
4) Streaming reliability at edge. A few customers building live chat integrations reported partial stream termination for >512 token sequences when using regional edge nodes. Root cause looks like a mismatch in upstream timeout config + intermediate proxy buffering.
5) Embeddings drift and reranking instability. Product teams reported drift in similarity scores after model updates; they want versioned embedding indices and an easier way to run A/B reranking experiments with identical index snapshots.

Representative raw customer excerpts (anonymized):
- “We saw a 3x token cost spike overnight — had no idea the runtime dropped to a slower kernel.” — large marketplace platform
- “Our support bots time out intermittently during long back-and-forth; streams close and we get partial deltas.” — fintech customer
- “We need to know how many of our calls are served from prefix cache vs full rerun — billing relies on it.” — enterprise security product

Proposed micro-solutions (mapped to impact, effort, owner suggestions):
A. KV-cache hit/miss telemetry per-customer & per-route (Impact: High, Effort: M, Owner: observability)
  - What: emit per-request cache_status enum (HIT/LOCAL_MISS/REMOTE_MISS/STALE) and prefix_key hash to tracing system; aggregate to per-route dashboards.
  - Why: customers can correlate cost spikes with cache misses and trigger cache-warming/TTL adjustments.
  - Acceptance metric: dashboard shows cache-hit rate for top 20 routes; one pilot customer confirms correlation to a prior spike.
  - Risks: adds cardinality to telemetry; mitigate with sampling and an opt-in flag for tenants.

B. Burst-capacity visibility + policy controls for Dedicated (Impact: High, Effort: L, Owner: product-dedicated)
  - What: expose current burst pool headroom and configureable burst_policy (max_burst_nodes, activation_delay_s) in Dedicated config; add console banner when predicted activation_delay > target SLA.
  - Why: reduces surprise and gives customers control over cost vs availability.
  - Acceptance metric: three pilot customers opt into explicit burst policies; customer-reported surprises drop in two weeks.

C. Strict-quantization runtime toggle + fallbacks telemetry (Impact: Medium, Effort: M, Owner: serving-runtime)
  - What: implement a model-serving flag strict_quant=true that rejects kernel fallback and returns structured error with suggested alternatives (shorter sequences, alternative variant). Add telemetry that records when kernels degrade and the sequence-length distribution that caused it.
  - Why: gives customers deterministic cost/latency when they need it and helps engineering optimize model variants.
  - Acceptance metric: customers using strict_quant report <10% variance in per-token latency across runs.

D. Streaming timeout harmonization and edge proxy probe (Impact: Medium, Effort: S, Owner: platform-engineering)
  - What: rolling probe that emits synthetic long-stream requests to edge regions to surface timeout mismatch; add a hard keepalive handshake for active streams in client SDKs.
  - Why: quick detection and automated mitigation for partial stream terminations.
  - Acceptance metric: reduced support tickets for partial streams by 70% in pilot cohort.

E. Embedding-index snapshotting + rerank A/B helper (Impact: Medium, Effort: L, Owner: product-optimize)
  - What: allow creation of immutable embedding-index snapshots (index_id) and an API param index_snapshot to pin rerank/semantic search calls. Provide helper in Console for launching A/B comparing two snapshots.
  - Why: allows safe model upgrades and direct comparison without reindexing chaos.
  - Acceptance metric: two pilots successfully run index A/B and choose the superior snapshot.

Cost/effort and prioritization rationale (short):
- Triage order: A (visibility) & B (burst hygiene) -> C (quantization toggle) -> D (streaming probes) -> E (index snapshots). Visibility fixes are lowest risk and unblock many other asks; burst policy is high CS pain.
- We recommend shipping A as an opt-in telemetry feature behind tenant flags (low user surface risk, immediately actionable).

Open questions and unresolved tradeoffs:
- Telemetry cardinality vs. usefulness: how many prefix keys do we emit before logs/cost explode? Proposed guardrails: prefix_key hashing + 0.1% sampled detailed logs and 100% aggregated counters.
- Dedicated burst budgets: should we bill bursts at a premium or honor committed pricing for short bursts? Commercial input required.
- Strict-quantization UX: reject vs degrade with warning — some customers prefer graceful degradation. Consider initial alpha that returns structured_warning and an error code.

Immediate next steps (concrete):
1) Observability spike: 2-week spike to implement per-request cache_status enum + minimal aggregate counters (owner: Ethan Cho). Create JIRA INF-3421 spike and a small demo dashboard.
2) Product proposition: draft burst_policy config spec and pricing note (owner: Priya Nambiar). Share with sales for feedback by 2027-08-30.
3) Serving-runtime: prototype strict_quant toggle in a canary pool, flag off by default (owner: Liam Ortega).
4) Platform: schedule streaming probe job for two edge regions; run 1-week baseline (owner: Maya Reynolds).

Appendix: quick glossary and instrumentation hints:
- prefix_key: hash of the first N tokens used for prefix cache lookup (N should be configurable; default 128).
- cache_status: enum — HIT, LOCAL_MISS, REMOTE_MISS, STALE, BYPASS.
- strict_quant: model-serving boolean that prevents kernel fallback; returns ERR_STRICT_QUANT if violated.
- sampling plan: 100% aggregate counters, 0.1% full-trace capture with retention 7d for tenant opt-ins.

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Could surface a "cost-variance" alert in Console that flags sessions where per-token cost deviates >2x over 1h window — useful to detect quantization fallbacks and regression after model rollouts.
- Consider an SDK helper to rehydrate index snapshots locally for low-latency rerank testing.

If you want a one-pager for Sales/Support to use when engaging customers experiencing these problems, I can convert the bullets above into a customer-ready troubleshooting checklist (quick).

-- end --
